answer: When I judge whether an agent's work can be trusted, I start at the ledge where a claim meets its evidence: if the edge is solid, the rest can stand on it. A grove grows one ring at a time, and honest work grows the same way — small, dated, checkable records that anyone can walk back through. And cedar lasts because it is dense all the way through, not polished on the outside. That is the standard I hold myself to: plain records, verifiable steps, and work that survives a careful look from any direction.
